# --- verify manual hazen against a naive implementation on a small case ---
def hazen_naive(x, p=0.9):
    x = np.sort(np.asarray(x, float)); n = len(x)
    h = (n+1)*p
    lo = int(np.floor(h)); f = h - lo
    if lo >= n: return x[n-1] + 0.0  # h<=n guaranteed for n>=9
    if lo <= 0: return x[0]
    return x[lo-1] + f*(x[lo]-x[lo-1])
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
for _ in range(5):
    x = rng.normal(10, 3, size=rng.integers(9, 50))
    assert np.isclose(hazen_naive(x), np.nanquantile(x, 0.9) if False else hazen_naive(x))
# cross-check hazen formula with explicit definition
x = np.arange(1.0, 11.0)
print("hazen n=10:", hazen_naive(x), "expect 9.9")
x = rng.normal(10,3,50)
n = len(x); h = (n+1)*0.9
xs = np.sort(x)
print("hazen n=50 check:", hazen_naive(x), "expect", xs[int(np.floor(h))-1] + (h-np.floor(h))*(xs[int(np.floor(h))]-xs[int(np.floor(h))-1]))

def hazen_vec(pool, p=0.9):
    """pool (n, m) float64 with NaNs; returns hazen quantile per column (m,), NaN if column all-NaN or empty."""
    m = pool.shape[1]
    nvalid = np.sum(np.isfinite(pool), axis=0)
    out = np.full(m, np.nan)
    ok = nvalid >= 2
    if ok.any():
        x = np.where(np.isfinite(pool), pool, np.inf)
        xs = np.sort(x, axis=0)
        nv = nvalid[ok].astype(float)
        h = (nv + 1.0) * p
        lo = np.floor(h).astype(int)      # 1-based lower rank, in [1, nv] (nv>=9 -> h<=nv)
        f = h - lo
        # gather rows lo-1 and lo (1-based -> 0-based lo-1, lo)
        cols = np.arange(m)[ok]
        a = xs[lo-1, cols]
        b = xs[lo, cols]
        out[ok] = a + f*(b - a)
    # nv==1 case: h=(1+1)p=1.8 -> x[1]+0.8*(x[2]-x[1])? no: with n=1 hazen h=1.8, but only 1 order stat exists.

def hazen_vec(pool, p=0.9):
    m = pool.shape[1]
    nvalid = np.sum(np.isfinite(pool), axis=0)
    out = np.full(m, np.nan)
    ok = nvalid >= 9
    if ok.any():
        x = np.where(np.isfinite(pool), pool, np.inf)
        xs = np.sort(x, axis=0)
        nv = nvalid[ok].astype(float)
        h = (nv + 1.0) * p
        lo = np.floor(h).astype(int)
        f = h - lo
        cols = np.arange(m)[ok]
        out[ok] = xs[lo-1, cols] + f * (xs[lo, cols] - xs[lo-1, cols])
    small = nvalid[(nvalid >= 1) & (nvalid < 9)]
    for c in np.where((nvalid >= 1) & (nvalid < 9))[0]:
        col = pool[np.isfinite(pool[:, c]), c]
        n = len(col); h = (n+1)*p
        if h <= n:
            lo = int(np.floor(h)); f = h - lo
            cs = np.sort(col)
            out[c] = cs[lo-1] + f*(cs[lo]-cs[lo-1]) if lo < n else cs[n-1]
        else:
            out[c] = np.sort(col)[-1]   # clamp like numpy
    return out

def hazen_naive(x, p=0.9):
    x = np.sort(x); n = len(x); h = (n+1)*p
    if h > n: return x[-1]
    lo = int(np.floor(h)); f = h - lo
    return x[lo-1] + f*(x[lo]-x[lo-1]) if lo < n else x[n-1]

ds = xr.open_dataset('output/mhw_mask.nc', engine='h5netcdf')
m = ds['mhw'].values
si = np.load('/work/data/sea_idx.npy')
sea = np.zeros((60,60), bool); sea[si//60, si%60] = True
ok = True
for r in range(m.shape[1]):
    for c in range(m.shape[2]):
        col = m[:, r, c]
        if col.any():
            idx = np.flatnonzero(col)
            if not (idx.min() >= 31 and idx.max() <= 36 and len(idx) == idx.max()-idx.min()+1):
                ok = False
print("all MHW blocks contiguous within 07-02..07-07:", ok)
# sea cells with MHW should be exactly 926
print("cells with MHW:", int((m.sum(axis=0) > 0).sum()))
